analysis.title: Nothing Good Happens Below the 200 DMA
key_insights: SPX is on track for a sixth straight daily decline and sits below its 200 DMA. BTIG cites Paul Tudor Jones: 'Nothing good happens below the 200 DMA', and notes the rule fails at the eventual bottom of corrections and bear markets.

In the last 30 years there were three prior 6-day losing streaks closing below the 200 DMA by no more than 3%: 9/27/00, 10/11/18 and 2/27/20. All three saw SPX higher five days later, then meaningful downside after the small bounce.
BTIG has targeted SPX 7,000-7,100. The intraday low of 7,193 is approaching that range.

The decline has not yet shown a sustained correlation-one move: downside volume was 74% as of about 1:00pm and AAPL was down less than 1%. BTIG expects a move closer to 7,000 before the selloff finishes.
With Thanksgiving approaching, a small bounce into next week would not be surprising. BTIG would use that strength to fade it, anticipating another leg lower.

Large-cap healthcare (XLV) is cracking. It had reached a 19% spread above its 200 DMA, and is now down 5.7% over four days, its largest such move since April 2025. BTIG sees more near-term downside toward $170-$175 before risk/reward turns more neutral.

BTIG is moving to the sidelines on precious metals after being cautious most of the year. Its gold downside target of about $3,500/oz is close, sentiment is washed out and tactical conditions are oversold. This is not a reversal to a constructive stance.
